summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia and other bypass-related issues was admitted to the surgery service for planned gastric bypass reversal. She underwent laparoscopic bypass reversal without intraoperative adverse events, recovered with initial NPO status and gastrostomy tube to gravity for decompression, and had a postoperative upper GI study showing no leak or obstruction. Pain control progressed from epidural to PCA and then to oral hydromorphone once she tolerated diet; her G-tube was clamped on postoperative day 3 and her diet was advanced sequentially to a Stage III diet with close monitoring of blood glucose, intake, and output. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable without evidence of infection or bleeding, ambulated independently, and was discharged home with instructions on Stage III diet, wound care with staples to be removed at follow-up, avoidance of NSAIDs, crushed pills, glucose monitoring with PRN glucose gel for hypoglycemia, and appropriate medications for pain, nausea, reflux prophylaxis, and constipation prevention.
